pr.title: Fix projections when parent capture is by-ref but child capture is by-value in the `ByMoveBody` pass

analysis.originalLogic: In the `ByMoveBody` MIR pass (`compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs`), for each parent/child capture pairing the code computed the extra child capture projections by slicing off the parent's projection prefix: `let child_precise_captures = &child_capture.place.projections[parent_capture.place.projections.len()..];`. It only added a deref-peeling adjustment when `child_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref()` (`let needs_deref = child_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref();`), and it stored the projection slice plus a `needs_deref: bool` in `field_remapping`. Nothing inserted a leading `Deref` when the *parent* capture was by-ref.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: When the parent coroutine-closure captured a place by-ref (so its upvar type was `&&Ty`) but the child coroutine captured the same logical place by-value (upvar type `&Ty`), the generated by-move body reused the parent capture's projections without inserting the extra leading `Projection { ty: parent_capture.place.ty(), kind: ProjectionKind::Deref }`. The resulting MIR assignment had mismatched types: `left-hand side has type: Ty` and `right-hand side has type: &Ty`, which under `-Zvalidate-mir` is reported as `broken MIR in CoroutineKindShim { coroutine_def_id:`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs using `#![feature(async_closure)]` where an `async` coroutine-closure passed to a `FnMut`/`Fn` consumer has a parent capture by reference of a non-`Copy` type, while the inner child coroutine captures by value because the body moves out of that shared reference. Example shape: `struct Ty;` (non-`Copy`), `fn hello(x: &Ty) { let c = async || { *x; }; }` or `impl Ty { fn hello(self) {} }` called as `x.hello()` inside the async closure. With `-Zvalidate-mir` this shows up as an ICE; semantically the program is expected to fail borrowck with E0507. If `Ty` were `Copy`, the child would capture by-ref instead and the bug would not trigger.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix in the `ByMoveBody` coroutine MIR pass: when the parent capture is by-ref but the child capture is by-value, the pass must insert a leading `Deref` projection to convert the parent's upvar type into the child's; otherwise the generated coroutine-kind-shim body contains a type-incorrect assignment and validation ICEs (issue #129074). The fix also replaces the old `needs_deref` condition with explicit `peel_deref` handling for child-by-ref and always validates the generated body.
analysis.trigger: A coroutine-closure's parent capture is by-ref while the child coroutine's capture for the same place is by-value. The child becomes by-value specifically because the body moves a non-`Copy` value out from behind a shared reference, so parent upvar type is `&&Ty` while child upvar type is `&Ty`.
preconditions: `#![feature(async_closure)]` async coroutine-closure whose by-move body is generated by the ByMoveBody pass
Parent coroutine-closure captures a place by reference (`parent_capture.is_by_ref()` true)
Child coroutine captures the corresponding place by value (`child_capture.is_by_ref()` false), typically from moving a non-Copy value out of a `&` reference
The captured pointee type is non-Copy; with a Copy type the child would instead capture by-ref and this path would not trigger
Observed as an ICE when compiling with `-Zvalidate-mir`; the underlying generated MIR is type-incorrect even without validation
pitfalls: Do not conflate the parent-by-ref fix (inserting a leading Deref into `child_precise_captures`) with the child-by-ref `peel_deref` adjustment (removing a trailing Deref from the child body); they are separate conditions.

The old `needs_deref = child_capture.is_by_ref() && !parent_capture.is_by_ref()` is not equivalent to the new `peel_deref = child_capture.is_by_ref()` with an assertion; when the parent is also by-ref you still need to both insert a leading deref and potentially peel a trailing one when precise capture projections exist.

Do not assume the bug is only about validation: the MIR is malformed (`Assign` with incompatible `Ty` vs `&Ty`) and the added `validate_body` call makes this detectable; the PR states it 'almost certainly results in a move error in borrowck' but 'let's not ICE'.

`FnOnce` coroutine-closures returning coroutines that capture from their body always produce a borrowck error in the peel case; the new assertion codifies `parent_capture.is_by_ref() || coroutine_kind != ty::ClosureKind::FnOnce`.
Changing the captured type to `Copy` masks the trigger by changing child capture mode, so tests must keep the struct non-Copy.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test (as in `tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/move-out-of-ref.rs`) with `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir`, `//@ edition: 2021`, `#![feature(async_closure)]`, a non-`Copy` `struct Ty;`, and a function taking `x: &Ty` that constructs `async || { *x; }` or calls a by-value `self` method. Assert the diagnostic is the expected borrowck error `E0507: cannot move out of `*x` which is behind a shared reference` rather than an ICE; check the `.stderr` fixture. Build two variants differing only in the transformation-relevant capture: parent by-ref + child by-value non-Copy (trigger) versus a Copy-typed pointee or by-value parent (non-trigger), to isolate the condition.
evidence: we weren't applying an additional deref projection to convert the parent capture into the child capture
If the parent capture is by-ref, then we need to apply an additional
